THIS MFA IS FILED U/S.173(1) OF MV ACT, PRAYING TO MODIFY THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 12.09.2018 PASSED BY THE SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS TRIBUNAL, CHINTHAMANI IN MVC NO.62/2014 AND TO PASS SUCH OTHER ORDER OR ORDERS AS THIS HON'BLE COURT DEEMS FIT UNDER THE FACTS AND CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE, INCLUDING THE COSTS, IN THE INTEREST OF JUSTICE AND EQUITY.
 THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THROUGH PHYSICAL HEARING/VIDEO CONFERENCING THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

Aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 12.09.2018 passed in MVC No.62/2014 by the Senior Civil Judge & JMFC, Chintamani (for short 'the Tribunal'), the respondent therein has preferred this appeal.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to herein as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are as follows:
That on 25.03.2014 at about 3.00 p.m. the deceased was riding the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-53-L-4832 near Bushettihalli to Peresandra service road,
Chickballapura Taluk and District, at that time the APSRTC bus bearing registration No.AP-02-Z-116 being driven in a rash and negligent manner came and dashed against the said motor cycle because of which the rider expired.
The petitioners being the dependants / legal heirs of the deceased preferred MVC No.62/2014.
4. The Tribunal based on the pleadings and evidence led-in has determined the compensation at Rs.12,85,000/-.

However, it concluded that the offending bus was responsible to an extent of 90% in causing the accident and another 10% was due to the negligent of motor bike and accordingly,
awarded compensation of Rs.11,56,500/- payable from respondent to the petitioners along with interest at 9% per annum from the date of petition till the amount is deposited with the Tribunal.
5. Aggrieved by the same, the respondent has preferred this appeal.
The petitioners have not preferred any appeal.
6. Respondent has preferred the instant appeal on the ground that the accident was due to the negligence on the part of the deceased and that the compensation awarded is excessive.

7. With regard to the first contention that negligence was on the part of the deceased, the respondent submits that the petitioners have not produced the driving licence of the deceased.
However, with regard to the accident, it is not in a position to dispute the fact that the accident happened due to the rash and negligent driving of the bus.
8. The case of the petitioners is that the deceased had the driving licence, but as he died in the accident, the same could not be found by his legal heirs and produce it before the Tribunal.

As the petitioners did not produce the driving licence of the deceased, the Tribunal has attributed 10%
negligence on the part of the deceased - rider of the motor bike.
The said 10% is attributed solely on the ground that the licence has not been produced and not because he drove the motor bike in a rash and negligent manner.

9. Under the given peculiar facts and circumstances of the case, I am of the opinion that the decision arrived at by the Tribunal in attributing 10% negligence to the rider of the motor bike and 90% to the rider of the bus is just and reasonable.
10.
The second contention of the respondent is that the Tribunal has taken the income of the deceased at Rs.9,000/- per month and the same is excessive.
The accident is of the year 2014.
Admittedly, the petitioners have not established the income of the deceased before the Tribunal.
The notional income as per the Lok Adalath chart ought to have been Rs.8,500/- per month.
The Tribunal has taken a sum of Rs.9,000/- as his notional income, which in my opinion is excessive.

However, if the decision of the Apex Court in Sarla Verma & Ors vs Delhi Transport Corp.& Anr [2009(6) SCC 121] and National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680], is taken into consideration with regard to multiplier and future prospects, then in that event, I find the compensation determined by the Tribunal is not excessive.

sentences.text: The appellant is not in a position to dispute this aspect and fairly concedes that though the Tribunal has taken the notional income at higher side, the final compensation granted is just and reasonable.
11. For the aforementioned reasons, I find no merit in the appeal filed by the respondent and accordingly, the appeal is hereby dismissed.
The amount in deposit if any, be transferred to the concerned Tribunal for disbursement.
Pending interlocutory applications, if any, do not survive for consideration and the same are hereby disposed of.
